:::{#exm-cauchy-sequence}
#### A Cauchy sequence of real numbers

The real numbers $\reals$ with the inner product $\iprod{x}{y} = x\,y$ form an inner product space,
and $\norm{x} = \abs{x}$ in it.
The sequence $x_n = \frac{1}{n}$ is a Cauchy sequence.
Given $\tolout > 0$, take $N$ to be any natural number larger than $\frac{1}{\tolout}$.
For all $m, n \ge N$, both $\frac{1}{m}$ and $\frac{1}{n}$ lie in $(0, \frac{1}{N}]$,
so $\abs{\frac{1}{m} - \frac{1}{n}} < \frac{1}{N} < \tolout$.
For example, with $\tolout = 0.01$, take $N = 101$:
all $m, n \ge 101$ have $\abs{\frac{1}{m} - \frac{1}{n}} < \frac{1}{101} < 0.01$.
